## Course Description

Fundamental concepts, techniques, and applications of risk assessment and risk management for engineering systems; current industry practices for risk assessment of industrial facilities using qualitative and quantitative approaches are demonstrated through exercises and case studies from diverse engineering fields.

## Special Course Designation

None

## Course Learning Outcomes

Upon completion of this course, the learner will be able to:

- Comprehend and articulate the fundamental goals and methodologies of the Systems Engineering discipline.

- Operate proficiently with international standards governing Systems Engineering and Risk Management.

- Conduct a comprehensive risk analysis, including the identification and assessment of potential hazards, to develop effective mitigation strategies.

- Develop and interpret probabilistic risk assessments for intricate engineering systems.

- Evaluate and model the reliability of individual engineering components and complex, interconnected systems.

## Textbook and/or Resource Materials

This material Is: Required
Reliability and Risk Analysis
ISBN: 9781000864137
Authors: Mohammad Modarres, Katrina Groth
Publisher: CRC Press
Publication Date: 2023-04-26

## Grading Policy

Quizzes, homework, assignments (20%)

Unit 1 Evaluation: Systems Engineering (20%)

Unit 2 Evaluation: Risk Management (20%)

Unit 3 Evaluation

: Probabilistic Risk Assessment - PRA (10%)

Unit 4 Evaluation

: Reliability (30%)

[90%,100%] gets an A, [80%,90%) gets a B, [70%,80%) gets a C, [60%, 70%) gets a D, and less than 60% gets an F.

Evaluations will be administered at the end of each module.

## Late Work Policy

Work submitted by a student as makeup work for an excused absence is not considered late work and is exempt from the late work policy (Student Rule 7).

## Course Specific Late Work Policy

No late work will be accepted.
